text:
Alex G: Heads up — two private VPC customers (tickets #4521, #4529) reported GPU init errors after a base OS security patch. Error shows 'cuInit: unknown error' when our containers try to initialize CUDA. They applied kernel 5.19.7 -> 5.19.9 and vendor driver changes around the same time.

Priya S: Can you paste the exact node logs and the output of basic checks? Are they running our recommended driver matrix or a vendor-provided shim?

Alex G: Logs from one node: 
```
[ 12:11:03 ] cuda: cuInit returned 999
[ 12:11:03 ] nvidia: failed to load kernel module: version mismatch
[ 12:11:04 ] container: fallback to cpu
```
Customer ran:
```bash
uname -r: 5.19.9-custom
modinfo nvidia | grep version: version: 535.86
/usr/bin/nvidia-smi --query-gpu=driver_version --format=csv,noheader: 535.67
```
So host kernel module (modinfo) and userland reported by nvidia-smi disagree.

Mike L: That's classic driver module drift — DKMS/vendor packaging built a different module than the userland driver. The host has module 535.86 but the runtime libs come from 535.67. That will cause cuInit failures.

Elly T: Telemetry shows NCCL error spikes for those same customers (lots of ERR_NO_DEVICE and "Driver/library version mismatch" log lines). I suspect some nodes have partial upgrades. Also seeing missing libnccl.so warnings in container logs.

Jordan-CS: Customer notes that doing `sudo modprobe -r nvidia && sudo modprobe nvidia` temporarily fixed one node, but after reboot the issue returned. They're on a RHEL-deriv with a custom kernel and vendor kernel-ml.

InfraBot: INC-2026-178 created — "host-driver-module-mismatch" detected for eu-west-1-private. Affected nodes: 8. Notified eng-infra + cs.

Priya S: Short term: can we give CS a tiny preflight script to run on customer hosts to surface this? We need uname, modinfo, packaged driver vs container driver, and ldconfig output. Also a human-readable explanation they can send.

Mike L: I'll draft a small script. Example snippet: 
```bash
#!/bin/bash
echo "kernel=$(uname -r)"
echo "modinfo_nvidia=$(modinfo nvidia | grep ^version: || true)"
echo "nvidia_smi=$(which nvidia-smi && nvidia-smi --query-gpu=driver_version --format=csv,noheader || true)"
echo "ldd_nccl=$(ldd /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libnvidia-ml.so 2>/dev/null || true)"
```
It should detect mismatches and exit non-zero. I'll push to gist and CS can share.

Alex G: Product question — do we have a stance on supporting vendor-compiled driver builds that differ from the matrix? CS says some enterprise customers will not/cannot change vendor kernels. We need a clear "drift" support tier (supported but out of SLA) vs strictly supported matrix.

Elly T: Recommend adding a runtime flag that surfaces "host-driver-drift" in the Private Console (node-level) and a running count in telemetry. Also for quick mitigation we could ship a sidecar that LD_PRELOADs our packaged libnccl for container workloads — but that needs security review.

Jordan-CS: CS will run the preflight on both customers tonight and gather module versions and timestamps. If it recurs we will open escalation and ask customers about kernel vendor patches. We'll attach the outputs to tickets #4521/#4529.

Priya S: Action items: (1) Mike to publish preflight script + gist (ETA: EOD tomorrow). (2) Mike + Elly to add a telemetry flag (host-driver-drift) and console alert (priority low) — Priya will own the alert spec. (3) Alex to draft support policy language for "driver drift" and share with legal/solutions.

Mike L: Ack. Will push script and a PR for telemetry signal.

InfraBot: Reminder: 2026-03-19 17:00 UTC — triage call with Customer A booked (10am PT).

Alex G: Thanks all — keeping this thread as the single source for the two tickets. Jordan, please paste preflight outputs when available and flag recurring nodes.
